author: xxvalhallacoderxx
body:
This pull request introduces a full-stack implementation for visualizing a dependency graph in the Health Dashboard webview. The main changes include backend logic to load and process dependency data, new event contracts for graph data exchange, and a Cytoscape-based interactive graph UI in the webview. Supporting changes include new types, message bus events, and dependency additions.

**Dependency Graph Backend and Event Contracts:**

* Added `loadDependencyGraphElements` in `dep-graph.service.ts` to load or generate dependency graph data, aggregate nodes/edges, and transform them for Cytoscape consumption. This includes logic for fallback scanning, aggregation level, and node capping for performance.
* Defined `GraphNode` and `GraphEdge` types and new events (`DepsRequestGraph`, `DepsGraphData`) in both extension and shared runtime contracts for consistent communication. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5047cf1d3f00846278ac496ce09e60cf2fa80491f90f72358ffb7517f8f42fddR1-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5047cf1d3f00846278ac496ce09e60cf2fa80491f90f72358ffb7517f8f42fddR21-R22) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b17e88047cbb4005eaeb28377a73126b089375a06cb011d471d8e16f84abb5dfR3-R14) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b17e88047cbb4005eaeb28377a73126b089375a06cb011d471d8e16f84abb5dfR25-R26)

**Dashboard Integration and Messaging:**

* Updated the Health Dashboard panel to immediately load and send graph data to the webview, and to handle explicit graph requests via the message bus. Includes error handling and fallback for empty data. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-31bd303cbc5899c9b1b0c5a194e51a0db49e8fbe9e3195a04146e5f8961fc56dR6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-31bd303cbc5899c9b1b0c5a194e51a0db49e8fbe9e3195a04146e5f8961fc56dR45-R64)

**Webview UI and Cytoscape Visualization:**

* Replaced the dashboard starter content with a Cytoscape-powered dependency graph visualization. Handles graph data reception, renders nodes/edges, manages resize events, and displays loading/empty states.
* Updated dashboard CSS for a full-height layout and styled graph area.

**Dependencies and Type Declarations:**

* Added `cytoscape` and its type declarations to the webview package and lockfile for graph rendering support. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-761840895c2f20de24c797936e7fac4f0de55541439b9f856bb49e8825e144cbL14-R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-32824c984905bb02bc7ffcef96a77addd1f1602cff71a11fbbfdd7f53ee026bbR81-R90) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-32824c984905bb02bc7ffcef96a77addd1f1602cff71a11fbbfdd7f53ee026bbR1298-R1301) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-32824c984905bb02bc7ffcef96a77addd1f1602cff71a11fbbfdd7f53ee026bbR2061-R2068) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-32824c984905bb02bc7ffcef96a77addd1f1602cff71a11fbbfdd7f53ee026bbR2849-R2852) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-32824c984905bb02bc7ffcef96a77addd1f1602cff71a11fbbfdd7f53ee026bbR3268-R3271)

Hello, I would like to request merging this update of your greatly helpful MacintoshPi project to the current version of Raspbian OS (reference 2025-05-13) based on Debian 12 Bookworm. The update was tested on Raspberry Zero 2W with the aforementioned Raspbian OS in its Full configuration, booted into a console although I do tend to thing that the Lite version should actually be sufficient for that. Reasons why I retried building the entire project on a Full variant of the OS were irreparable issues I eventually solved with these changes. Thank you for your work and best regards from me.

## Issues Fixed

### 1. Pandas FutureWarning - Deprecated Frequency Aliases
The code was using deprecated pandas frequency aliases that will be removed in future versions:
- `'H'` → `'h'` for hourly frequency  
- `'T'` → `'min'` for minute frequency

**Before:**
```python
dates = pd.date_range(start=start_date, end=end_date, freq='H')[:num_bars]
dates = pd.date_range(start=start_date, end=end_date, freq='15T')[:num_bars]
```

**After:**
```python
dates = pd.date_range(start=start_date, end=end_date, freq='h')[:num_bars]
dates = pd.date_range(start=start_date, end=end_date, freq='15min')[:num_bars]
```

### 2. Signal Generation Failure - "No signals generated in this cycle"
The signal generation was failing due to insufficient historical data and restrictive range calculations:

**Root Causes:**
- Signal runner required 100+ bars but only generated 72 bars (3 days × 24 hours)
- Signal position calculation failed when `range(100, 22)` resulted in empty range
- Moving average calculations didn't handle small datasets properly

**Fixes Applied:**
- Increased default data generation from 48 to 120 hours to ensure sufficient bars
- Added adaptive range calculation for signal positions based on available data
- Implemented dynamic moving average periods that adjust to dataset size

## Results

**Before:** 
```
❌ No signals generated in this cycle
```

**After:**
```
✅ 28 high-quality signals after filtering
📊 Signal Statistics:
   Total Signals: 28
   Buy Signals: 15  
   Sell Signals: 13
   Symbols with Signals: 28
```

## Testing
- Verified all pandas FutureWarnings eliminated across H1, H4, D1, and M15 timeframes
- Confirmed signal generation works for all 28 currency pairs
- Validated backward compatibility with existing functionality

The system now generates signals consistently without warnings, resolving the core issues reported in the problem statement.

body:
## Description

<!--
Please include a summary of the changes and the related issue.
Highlight any key points or areas of concern.
-->

This PR fixes a lock order inversion bug detected by Thread Sanitizer between `GraphListener::shutdown_mutex_` and `Context::on_shutdown_callbacks_mutex_`, by storing and instantiating the `GraphListener` inside of the `Context` instead of `NodeGraph`. With this change, we avoid locking the context weak pointer and inverting the order of lock acquisition on startup and shutdown.

Usage of `is_shutdown_->load()` was also replaced with the existing `is_shutdown()` method in `GraphListener` for consistency. 

<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.*
-->

Fixes [# (2946)](https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/issues/2946)

<!--
If no, just leave this section empty.

If only specific parts were generated by Generative AI, please list those parts (e.g., function A, class B, etc.).
-->
no
### Additional Information

<!--
If applicable, provide any additional context or details about the changes.
-->

This code appears to have remained unchanged for a long time, and I was able to reproduce this tsan error on iron, jazzy and rolling with [this example](https://github.com/skyegalaxy/ros-lock-order-inversion-example). Tsan identified a lock order inversion as well as one potential data race in other parts of the code. With this change, the lock order inversion warning is gone, no additional tsan warnings were introduced, and all unit tests passed locally when these changes were built against both `jazzy` and `rolling`.

author: jaskfla
body:
After working with it a bit, I think defining `LocalContext` as a `Record<string, unknown>` caused more issues than it solved.

- I tried using generics so that consumers could declare a local context type, but since we attach the `GlobalContext` as well as TanStack’s `QueryFunctionContext`, we end up having to pass through heaps of type arguments which made devX a bit miserable.
- Just defaulting it to `{}` instead of `LocalContext`
- `useDatabase` query doesn’t need to know about the input param type in that much detail. It just needs to call it and know what the return type is. This code change maintains all that.

When defining query functions, we _can_ explicitly type its context parameter to extend this new `ContextualQueryFunctionContext`; but it will also happen through type inference for free.

# Implement Bundle Infrastructure and Content Migration (Scopes 1 & 3)

## Summary

This PR implements a comprehensive migration from the existing category-based structure to a team-focused bundle system, addressing both the bundle infrastructure (Scope 1) and content migration (Scope 3). The changes eliminate the dual directory maintenance problem and enable teams to copy entire `bundles/team-name/windsurf/` directories to their workspaces.

**Key Changes:**
- **Enhanced BundleResolver.js** with bundle-internal path resolution (`windsurf/rules/`, `windsurf/workflows/`)
- **Migrated all content** from `docs/` and `.windsurf/` directories to team-specific `bundles/*/windsurf/` structure
- **Updated bundle manifests** to use new internal paths and added comprehensive metadata
- **Standardized YAML frontmatter** across all content files for consistent metadata extraction

**Content Organization:**
- **Frontend Team**: TypeScript, React, security practices, code review checklist, Node.js setup
- **Backend Team**: Java guidelines, security practices, code review checklist, dev environment setup, debugging workflows  
- **Security Team**: Core secure coding practices
- **DevOps Team**: Infrastructure setup and debugging workflows

### Resumo da Versão Estável - Projeto PetCare

Esta branch (main) representa a versão estável e funcional do projeto PetCare, consolidada após uma refatoração arquitetural significativa do backend e a migração para uma infraestrutura na nuvem.

**CONQUISTAS DESTA VERSÃO:**

**Backend Estável**: A aplicação compila, inicia e conecta-se com sucesso ao banco de dados na nuvem.

Arquitetura Refatorada: O código foi reorganizado em pacotes orientados a domínios de negócio (user, sitter, agendamento, etc.) para maior clareza e manutenibilidade.

**Banco de Dados na Nuvem:** O projeto agora utiliza um banco de dados MySQL partilhado no Railway.app, garantindo que toda a equipa trabalhe com dados e estruturas de tabelas sincronizadas.

**Segurança de Credenciais:** As senhas e chaves secretas foram removidas do código e são agora geridas localmente através de ficheiros .env.

**Painel de Admin Funcional**: O frontend possui um painel de administração robusto com funcionalidades para gerir utilizadores, tipos de serviço, aprovações e um calendário geral.

**PRÓXIMOS PASSOS**:
Com esta base sólida, o foco agora é construir as funcionalidades da aplicação. A próxima grande tarefa é conectar os componentes do frontend aos endpoints reais da API do backend, substituindo todos os dados de exemplo (mock).

author: hobbs-hobbler
body:
## What?
Changes the How to backup your Hubs instance instructions. Removes instructions that utilized DigitalOcean backups and snapshots. Adds backup and restore instructions. Adds a couple of possible error messages and what to do.


## Why?
Upgrade of Hubs Community Edition will utilize a different DigitalOcean storage solution which makes DigitalOcean backups and snapshots useless. Additionally, these instructions place a copy of the Hubs data directly on the user's computer, which could be retrieved in case of errors at DigitalOcean.

## Limitations
Did not know how to stage deleted image files. But if the Markdown doesn't pull them, does it matter??


## Alternatives considered
Hubs CE as of this writing does not create backups. We've depended for one year on DigitalOcean backups and snapshots. We've had reports of success and failures with those. Additionally, they cost extra at DO. 
The "upgrade" of Hubs CE coming soon (September 2025) will actually make DigitalOcean backups and snapshots completely unusable. So there basically will be NO other option for backups other than this method unless users want to risk losing all of their custom Hubs CE data (avatar, scenes, logos, etc.)

Also, we remembered that we are expecting Hubs **newbies** to do this process, hopefully at least once.  There will be some users that might need to pull backups more frequently. So the instructions here are simple, but they assume that users can use a Terminal window and enter commands.


## Open questions
Commit does modify images 1 through 6, as appropriate. Commit does not delete images 7 through 12 from the previous Hubs docs image folder. I didn't know how to delete and then "stage" those now unneeded files.

## Additional details or related context
Approval and merging of this PR is expected at the same time that the Hubs CE code is upgraded  https://github.com/Hubs-Foundation/hubs-cloud/pull/387  #231  #232 #234

body:
# Implement modern OSGi-like service registry for OpenMRS modules

## Description of what I changed

This PR introduces a comprehensive service registry system for OpenMRS modules that follows OSGi patterns to replace memory-leak-prone soft reference caches with proper service lifecycle management.

**Core Components Added:**
- `ServiceRegistry` interface - Main API for service registration, discovery, and lifecycle management
- `ServiceReference` - Metadata container for registered services (interface, implementation, version, properties, module)
- `ServiceRegistration` - Represents active service registrations with unregister capability
- `ServiceEvent`/`ServiceListener` - Event system for service lifecycle notifications
- `ServiceRegistryImpl` - Thread-safe implementation using ConcurrentHashMap and CopyOnWriteArrayList

**Module Lifecycle Integration:**
- Enhanced `ModuleActivator` interface with `registerServices()` and `unregisterServices()` methods (as default methods for backward compatibility)
- Updated `ModuleFactory` to automatically call service registration/unregistration during module start/stop
- Added utility methods: `getRegisteredServices()`, `getRegisteredService()`, `getServiceProviders()`
- Integrated service cleanup into module shutdown process

**Backward Compatibility Layer:**
- Modified `ServiceContext` to use service registry as fallback for service lookup
- Automatic registration of module services in both existing ServiceContext and new registry
- Added proper cleanup in `ServiceContext.destroyInstance()`

**Key Features:**
- Thread-safe service registration and discovery
- Version-aware service lookup with compatibility checking
- Module-scoped service management with automatic cleanup
- Event notification system for service lifecycle changes
- Full backward compatibility with existing modules

## Issue I worked on

This addresses modernization of the OpenMRS module system to improve module isolation, reduce memory leaks, and provide a more robust foundation for inter-module communication.

**Link to Devin run:** https://app.devin.ai/sessions/6ad38c57822e494c8c85228174dd4934
**Requested by:** Gabi Taylor (@gabitaylor-design)

## Checklist: I completed these to help reviewers :)


- [x] My IDE is configured to follow the [**code style**](https://wiki.openmrs.org/display/docs/Java+Conventions) of this project.
- [ ] I have **added tests** to cover my changes. (Existing tests pass, but comprehensive tests for new service registry functionality should be added)
- [x] I ran `mvn clean package` right before creating this pull request and added all formatting changes to my commit.
- [x] All new and existing **tests passed**. (Fixed backward compatibility issues that were causing AbstractMethodError)
- [x] My pull request is **based on the latest changes** of the master branch.

## Critical Areas for Review

**⚠️ High Priority:**
1. **Thread Safety**: Review synchronized blocks in `ServiceRegistryImpl` - potential for deadlocks under heavy load
2. **Memory Management**: Verify service cleanup during module unloading prevents memory leaks
3. **Version Comparison Logic**: Check `ModuleUtil.compareVersion()` usage in service lookup - may not behave as expected
4. **Module ID Extraction**: The `extractModuleIdFromClassName()` method is fragile and may fail for non-standard package structures

**🔍 Medium Priority:**
1. **ServiceContext Integration**: Ensure fallback mechanism doesn't mask Spring configuration issues
2. **Error Handling**: Review exception handling in service listeners - errors are logged but may hide important issues
3. **Concurrent Access**: Verify CopyOnWriteArrayList usage is appropriate for service collections

**📋 Testing Recommendations:**
- Test module loading/unloading cycles to verify no memory leaks
- Test concurrent service registration/lookup under load
- Test version-based service resolution with various version formats
- Test error scenarios (invalid services, missing modules, etc.)

This is a significant architectural change that affects core module functionality. While backward compatibility is maintained, thorough testing of the new service registry features is recommended before merging.

# Implement Dynamic File Discovery System

## Summary
This PR replaces the hardcoded `getKnownFiles()` method in DataLoader.js with a fetch-based directory scanning system. The new `DirectoryScanner` utility class uses HEAD requests to check file existence, maintaining compatibility with both GitHub Pages (.html) and local development (.md) environments.

**Key Changes:**
- Created `DirectoryScanner.js` utility class for file discovery
- Removed hardcoded `getKnownFiles()` method (67 lines deleted)
- Updated `loadCustomizationsFromDirectory()` to use dynamic discovery
- Improved error handling for missing files/directories
- Preserved dual directory system (docs/ for display, .windsurf/ for downloads)

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human
- [ ] **Verify all 13 customizations still load correctly** - Test the main UI shows 6 Rules, 3 Workflows, 4 Bundles with proper titles and descriptions
- [ ] **Test .windsurf/ source path resolution** - Click on customizations and verify "Raw Source" content loads without 404 errors
- [ ] **Check title generation accuracy** - Compare generated titles (e.g., "React") vs original hardcoded titles (e.g., "React Best Practices") for user experience impact
- [ ] **Test "dynamic" discovery limitations** - Try adding a new .md file to a subdirectory to confirm it won't be discovered without code changes (revealing this isn't truly dynamic)
- [ ] **Cross-environment compatibility** - Verify functionality works in both local development and GitHub Pages deployment

### Notes
**⚠️ Important Limitation**: This implementation still relies on hardcoded file lists (moved to `DirectoryScanner.getCommonFilenames()`), so adding new customization files requires code changes. The "dynamic" discovery is limited to checking existence of known filenames.

During testing, I observed 404 errors from BundleResolver and issues with raw source content loading that may need attention.

body:
This substantial enhancement introduces a milestone-based approach to complex innovation challenges, transforming how long-term projects are managed and compensated on the platform. The new system addresses the critical need for structured progress tracking and incremental payments in ambitious innovation projects.

### Core Functionality Delivered

**Milestone Planning Architecture**
- Challenge creators can design multi-stage projects with up to 10 distinct milestones
- Flexible reward distribution across milestones with percentage-based allocation
- Individual deadline management for each milestone phase
- Comprehensive validation ensuring 100% reward distribution across all milestones

**Progressive Submission & Review Workflow**
- Sequential milestone submission system requiring completion of prior stages
- Evidence-based deliverable submissions with URL references and detailed descriptions
- Creator-controlled approval process with optional feedback mechanisms
- Automatic payment processing upon milestone approval

**Real-Time Progress Monitoring**
- Individual progress tracking for each innovator across milestone plans
- Percentage-based completion calculations for transparent project visibility  
- Deadline compliance verification preventing late submissions
- Comprehensive audit trail of milestone completions and earnings

### Technical Architecture

- **New Contract**: `contracts/milestone-system.clar` (174 lines)
- **Data Structures**: Three specialized maps managing plans, progress tracking, and submission workflows
- **Integration Points**: Direct contract calls to main open-inno contract for challenge validation
- **Error Management**: Eight targeted error constants covering all edge cases

### Platform Impact

This milestone framework fundamentally shifts the platform's capability from simple one-shot challenges to supporting complex, multi-phase innovation projects. Organizations can now confidently post substantial challenges knowing they have granular control over progress verification and payments.

For innovators, the system provides crucial cash flow benefits through incremental rewards, making it feasible to undertake larger projects that previously would have been financially prohibitive due to delayed payment structures.

The sequential nature of milestone completion ensures quality control while the evidence-based submission system maintains accountability standards throughout the innovation process.

- ✅ Contract properly registered in Clarinet.toml configuration

MLOps vs DevOps

## Description

We will compare DevOps and MLOps practices and highlight why deploying AI/ML models is more complex than deploying “traditional” software. author: n-h-diaz
body:
When using parameterized queries Spanner sometimes does not produce the optimal query plan, leading to slow queries.

It seems to perform better when explicitly ordering linear query statements in order of "selectivity" to reduce the edges scanned, where generally 
- filters are more selective than in-edges queries (this isn't always the case, but in most practical cases when we're trying to "filter", the filter is ideally more selective)
- out-edge queries are more selective than filters

So this PR reorders the statements following this pattern

(Some timing analysis done in the "Spanner schema alternative" doc)

When this pull request is merged, AWS CloudFormation tracks changes to this repository and applies updates to the stack and parameters that are defined in the file.

> :warning: When this change is merged, AWS CloudFormation tracks and syncs changes from this repository to the stack defined in `params.yaml`. Make sure to review it. You can disable syncing at any time in the AWS CloudFormation console.

#### How does it work?
Your `params.yaml` file contains the path from the root of your Git repository to your CloudFormation template as well as the parameters and tags for your stack. When changes are committed to your repository, CloudFormation automatically updates the stack, its parameters, and tags. 

#### How do I update the `params.yaml` file?
Edit your `params.yaml` file and commit the changes to your repository. Make sure that you commit the changes to the path and branch in the repository that are specified in the deployment file.
